speaker: Doctor
text:
I need to understand the onset of these symptoms. Can you tell me when the aggressive behavior and altered mental status first started, and have you experienced any recent fever or severe headache?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Toxicology_Screen.

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient's roommates report that he has been displaying increasingly aggressive and unusual behavior. They mention that he has been under significant stress due to final exams and has become more reclusive. Earlier this evening, he exhibited extreme irritability, yelled at his computer, broke it, and then spent several hours at the gym.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive behavior and irritability. I also have Yelling, Breaking objects, Prolonged physical activity (several hours at the gym), Rapid speech during exam, Aggressiveness during exam.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history reported by the roommates. Social history: Stress from upcoming final exams. No other social history provided.

speaker: Patient
text: Roommates did not report any fever, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or flank pain prior to the event. During the physical exam, the patient is noted to be diaphoretic. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you been exposed to any chemicals or ingested any unknown substances recently?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Liver_Function_Tests, Arterial_Blood_Gas.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Negative for drug screen, no ketones, normal glucose. Liver_Function_Tests: ALT 28 U/L, AST 30 U/L, Bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 110 U/L (All Normal). Arterial_Blood_Gas: pH 7.48, pCO2 32 mmHg, pO2 98 mmHg, HCO3 24 mEq/L (Normal Acid-Base status).

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the normal toxicology screen and liver function, but the presence of autonomic instability (diaphoresis, altered mental status, and aggressive behavior), have you noticed any recent episodes of extreme anxiety, panic attacks, or specific triggers like social situations or performance demands?

REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Stimulating_Hormone, Free_T4.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: TSH: 0.8 mIU/L (Normal), Free T4: 1.1 ng/dL (Normal)

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since thyroid and metabolic causes are ruled out, have you had any recent head trauma, seizures, or witnessed any shaking movements during the episodes of aggression?

REQUEST TEST: Electroencephalogram (EEG), CT_Head.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide any available images of the patient's current physical exam or prior neurological history.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: EEG: Normal background activity, no epileptiform discharges. CT Head: No acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or signs of recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the exclusion of metabolic, toxic, endocrine, structural, and seizure-related causes for your altered mental status and autonomic dysregulation, did you experience any recent visual or auditory hallucinations, or a feeling of "unreality" (déjà vu/déjà vu) prior to the aggression?

REQUEST TEST: Antinuclear_Antibody (ANA), C-Reactive_Protein (CRP).
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide any available images of the patient's current physical exam or prior neurological history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you noticed any new-onset tremors, muscle stiffness, or swallowing difficulties, and did anyone witness the onset of these neurological symptoms?

REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase (CK), Cerebrospinal_Fluid_Lumbar_Puncture.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide MRI_Brain sequences if available.
